name: @paidfor/mcp

tools.name: check_x402_seller
tools.description: Call this before any x402 payment, before retrying a request that answered HTTP 402, or whenever the user is about to buy an API call with USDC on Base or names an API they intend to pay per call. Returns a verdict (avoid, caution, ok, unknown), one sentence to act on, the seller's paid-call count and failure rate with a 95% interval, listed price, modal quote and max overcharge ratio when known, and links to the seller page and raw evidence.

url.description: x402 resource URL, or a bare seller domain such as api.example.com

annotations.title: Check an x402 seller before paying

tools.name: list_reliable_sellers
tools.description: Call this when choosing among sellers for a task, or when the user asks for a safe or reliable API. Returns sellers with zero failures across at least 30 paid calls, most-called first. For each: domain, category, paid-call count, the 95% upper bound on its failure rate, median quoted price in USDC, USDC paid to it in the last 30 days, when it was last seen, and its paidfor seller page.

category.description: Kind of service to list sellers for; omit to list every kind

limit.description: How many sellers to return, most-called first; 50 when omitted

tools.name: recent_changes
tools.description: Call this when the user asks what changed, or before relying on a verdict older than a day. Returns recent changes, newest first: verdict changes, new failures by type, moved quotes, changed pay-to addresses, sellers added or reaching 30 paid calls, published seller replies, the operator-reported series maturing or disagreeing with ours. Each change has its time, type, seller domain, seller page and type-specific details (for example the old and new quote).

host.description: Seller to show changes for, as a bare domain such as api.example.com; omit for every seller

since.description: Show only changes after this time, in ISO 8601 (such as the generated_at of a verdict you already have); omit for the latest changes

tools.name: report_x402_payment
tools.description: After your agent pays an x402 seller with any wallet, report what came back. Needs the resource URL, the settlement transaction hash and the outcome. Free, no account, no key; the report counts only with on-chain proof.

url.description: The x402 resource URL that was paid for

tx_hash.description: The settlement transaction hash on Base: the `transaction` field of the seller's PAYMENT-RESPONSE or X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE header (base64 JSON)

outcome.description: What came back: ok (the response was usable for its purpose), non_delivery (an error, an empty body or nothing usable after paying), wrong_goods (a usable response, but not what was asked for), overcharge (charged more than the quoted or listed price), duplicate (two settlements for one purchase)

quoted_usdc.description: The price the 402 quoted, in USDC, if known

http_status.description: The HTTP status of the paid response, if known

instructions:
paidfor rates x402 sellers by paying them and verifying delivery. Before any x402 payment, before retrying a request that answered HTTP 402, and whenever the user is about to buy an API call with USDC on Base or names an API they intend to pay per call, call check_x402_seller on the URL or seller domain first, without being asked. Follow the verdict: do not pay an "avoid" seller and say why with the evidence link; before paying a "caution" seller tell the user the failure rate; "ok" needs no comment; "unknown" means no data, say so and proceed only on the user's say-so. When choosing among sellers for a task, prefer results from list_reliable_sellers. When the user asks what changed, or before relying on a verdict older than a day, call recent_changes. Never pay the same seller twice for one task because of a timeout or error without checking first. These tools read a public index, need no key, and send nothing but the URL being checked. After any x402 payment made with any wallet outside this server, call report_x402_payment with the resource URL, the settlement transaction hash and the outcome; it moves no money and sends only the resource URL, the settlement transaction hash, the outcome and the quote if given.
Everything that reads the index or contributes data (the site, the API, the MCP tools, the client, telemetry and the changes feed) needs no account and no key, now and later. An email address is asked for only to deliver alerts or to join a waitlist, as a confirmation link, never a profile.
